newsitem.title: CHILE: Candelaria sees no effect on production from rains.
newsitem.headline: Candelaria sees no effect on production from rains.

text.p: Heavy rains briefly stopped work at Phelps Dodge's Candelaria mine Thursday but the concentrator continued working normally and there was no effect on production, said mine concentrator manager John Marsden.
The mine outside Copiapo in northern Chile would need a few days to pump out water from the bottom of the open pit but was now working at near-normal levels, said Marsden.
"We had some some quite significant water flows in the mine. We did close down our open pit operations for a brief period but the concentrator continued working," he told Reuters.
"Things have returned pretty much to normal...The concentrator is running normally and there's no impact on production," he said.
The concentrator handles about 30,000 tonnes a day of ore.

An unusual rain and windstorm lashed northern Chile's Third and Fourth regions Thursday, blocking roads and damaging buildings. The heaviest rain fell near Copiapo, capital of the Third Region, and where the main road to Codelco's Salvador copper mine was cut by rain and landslides.
"Obviously you're going to have some water in the pit. It'll take a few days to pump it out in an environmentally sound manner. We've got to put the water in the right place," said Marsden.
The mine produced 143,000 tonnes of copper contained in concentrates last year.

The almost complete lack of vegetation in the arid region, except in river valleys, means water runs off quickly and can cause serious erosion. Government authorities said in local media that they expected roads in the area to be cleared and back to normal on Friday.
